title: Replace the obsolete Rhino engine with a modern JavaScript runtime (V8/Node, ES6+)
summary: Rhino lags modern JavaScript by years, so ES6+ syntax, npm libraries and online examples do not work in channel scripts. Users ask for V8/Node or at least every Rhino upgrade (template literals in 1.7.14); Rhino upgrades themselves caused regressions.
quote: Rhino has not aged well and is far behind modern JS.

title: Add optional chaining and other modern syntax to scripts
summary: Users want optional chaining (or a $t helper that emulates it) and class syntax, which Rhino lacks, to cut boilerplate when walking messages with missing fields.

title: Keep E4X-style XML/HL7 navigation when modernizing the script engine
summary: Channel scripts lean on E4X (msg['PID']['PID.5']) which only Rhino supports; strict parsing and validation changes broke E4X access. Proposals suggest emulating E4X with ES6 Proxy so a new engine stays compatible.

title: Stop Java strings leaking into JavaScript (wrapped primitives break ===, switch, replace)
summary: Values returned from Java APIs are Java objects, so strict equality, switch statements, array functions and String.replace behave unexpectedly. Users ask for a setting that converts Java primitives to JS primitives.

title: Pre-poll script for polling connectors to rotate targets/credentials per poll
summary: Polling sources cannot change host, directory or query before each poll, so users build one channel per endpoint (one user has 160 SFTP servers). A before-poll script, multiple dir/filter pairs and poll sourceMap variables are requested.
quote: I have 160 sftp servers I need to poll.

title: Trigger a poll on demand ("Poll now") and support run-once schedules
summary: Running a polling channel once requires editing poll-on-start, redeploying and reverting. Users want a dashboard "poll now" action and a never/run-once schedule; poll-on-start failures are not logged.

title: Built-in step-through debugger for channel scripts
summary: Debugging means logger statements and redeploys. NextGen mocked up a debugger (variables, maps, JVM stats); users asked for quick message injection, var types and thread dumps, then reported the shipped debugger failing to launch, missing locals and exhausting memory.

title: Better code editor: autocomplete for Java/3rd-party libs, configurable shortcuts, find/replace
summary: The script editor lacks autocomplete for Java and custom libraries, has awkward macOS keybindings and a limited find/replace. Users want an IDE-grade editor.

title: Script editor freezes the Administrator while editing JavaScript
summary: Editing loops in transformer JavaScript hangs the Administrator for years across versions; root cause traced to the closed-source launcher not draining the client process output, with launching via JNLP as a workaround.

title: Server-level startup/shutdown scripts and a global script preprocessor
summary: The "shutdown" script actually runs on undeploy; users want true server start/stop hooks plus a script preprocessor and an option to force-run compiled code templates.

title: Persist global maps across restarts
summary: Global and channel maps are memory-only and vanish on restart or redeploy, so state such as "last batch date" must be hand-persisted to a database or file.

title: Give global maps atomic ConcurrentMap operations (putIfAbsent, computeIfAbsent)
summary: Global map stores are backed by ConcurrentHashMap but do not expose atomic methods, so thread-safe counters and caches need custom synchronization.

title: Fix channel-reversed code template library dependencies
summary: Libraries list the channels that use them rather than channels declaring their libraries, which is unmanageable with hundreds of channels; API support for updating or deleting a single library is weak.

title: Isolate per-channel/extension libraries (classloader conflicts, child-first loading)
summary: Custom JARs collide with bundled library versions, extensions conflict, and custom-lib contents can stop listeners starting. Users asked for child-first resource loaders (added in 4.3), per-extension classloaders and loading JARs without UI steps.

title: Built-in lookup tables
summary: Users want native lookup/crosswalk tables managed in the engine instead of external databases or code templates.

title: Request a standard library for common healthcare chores (hashing, base64, JSON helpers)
summary: Users repeatedly ask how to hash messages, convert hex/base64 or POST with cURL from a transformer; they want utility methods built in.

title: HL7 v2 parsing/serialization quirks corrupt or alter messages
summary: Reports include the first tilde being dropped, MSH encoding characters escaped as entities, empty repeats leaving stray separators, field order changing output, null characters erroring and slow strict parsing of large encoded fields.

title: Character-encoding bugs across HTTP, database and web-service connectors
summary: Non-ASCII data is mangled by HTTP connectors and database reads, octet-stream payloads get corrupted, and 4.5 strips  in SOAP calls.

title: JSON to HL7 conversion is fragile
summary: Converting JSON to HL7 via the XML serializer throws parse errors, JSON strings lose characters, and multiple HL7 messages inside one JSON payload are hard to split.

title: Add X12/EDI data type support
summary: Users ask how to parse X12 EDI in the open-source engine, which lacks an obvious path.

title: Read Excel, Parquet and newer document formats; produce C-CDA
summary: Users want Parquet and Excel readers, CSV to C-CDA conversion and a bundled Apache POI new enough to work.

title: Delimited text should infer column names from a header row
summary: CSV handling uses positional column names; users want header-row field names and more forgiving fixed-length parsing.

title: Batch processing gaps (batchMap, JS batch on TCP, batch send)
summary: Batch scripts cannot share state per batch without global maps (which mix concurrent batches), JavaScript batch splitting fails with TCP sources, and position-in-batch is hard to get.

title: XSLT 2.0 / XPath 2.0 support
summary: Users ask for Saxon-based XSLT/XPath 2.0 rather than the bundled 1.0 processor.

title: Message templates and tree view fail to parse HL7 in the filter/transformer editor
summary: In 4.3 the message tree and templates stopped parsing HL7 v2, removing drag-and-drop mapping until fixed.

title: Modernize DICOM: dcm4che 5 and full SOP class coverage
summary: The DICOM stack is built on deprecated dcm4che2; missing SOP classes (ophthalmic, breast tomo) needed custom builds, some tags fail to parse or are lost, and attachments reattach out of order.

title: DICOM Worklist, Query/Retrieve and association reuse
summary: Users want modality worklist and C-FIND/query sources, and the sender reopens an association per instance (130 associations for one CT). A commercial DICOM extension was later offered instead.

title: Open-source FHIR support and HL7 v2 to FHIR conversion
summary: The FHIR connector is an extension whose source and usage are unclear, and users repeatedly ask how to map HL7 v2 or C-CDA to FHIR resources with no built-in mapping.

title: AMQP / RabbitMQ connector
summary: RabbitMQ works only through the JMS connector with extra client JARs and stripping the JMS envelope; users want a native AMQP reader/writer with proper ack semantics.

title: Cloud-native connectors: S3-compatible endpoints, AWS IAM roles, SQS, Azure Blob, Google Pub/Sub
summary: The S3 writer is locked to Amazon endpoints and static credentials, map variables do not refresh in it, and there is no SQS, Azure Blob or Pub/Sub support, so users hand-load cloud SDKs.

title: Kafka connector
summary: The JMS connector cannot talk to Kafka, and users ask about change-data-capture (Debezium) style sources.

title: SMB2/SMB3 and encrypted SMB support for file connectors
summary: SMB support long relied on SMB1-only JCIFS; users ask for SMBJ, report encrypted shares failing in 4.5.2, Java-version access errors and memory leaks.

title: Replace unmaintained JSch to fix SFTP algorithm negotiation failures
summary: The bundled JSch had no release since 2018 and cannot negotiate modern OpenSSH algorithms; users asked to swap in the maintained mwiede fork.

title: SFTP/FTP file connector reliability bugs
summary: Reports: SFTP writer overwrites despite "File Exists: Error", subdirectory recursion makes redundant calls or fails, file-age checks block reads, files vanish with no error dir, and key-file settings are misdocumented. Requests include FTPS, proxy support and "only if exists" post-actions.

title: Cron-style scheduling for polling and pruning
summary: Fixed-interval polling forced users to stop channels on weekends by hand; cron and weekday/time-window schedules were requested for years before landing in 3.3.

title: Show which server instance you are connected to
summary: With many environments open, users want the server name and logged-in user shown in the Administrator title bar to avoid editing the wrong system.

title: TCP Sender "server mode" and failover/alternate destinations
summary: Some EMRs expect the engine to listen for their connection before sending; users also want built-in alternate destinations when the primary fails.

title: TCP/MLLP connections error on stop/redeploy and leak sockets
summary: Keep-open sockets throw on stop/redeploy, the dispatcher leaves sockets open after undeploy, TLS via the SSL extension errors, and timeout noise cannot be suppressed.

title: Control MLLP ACK generation (invalid messages, custom ACK before processing)
summary: No ACK is returned for partially invalid messages, namespaced XML ACKs are not recognized, late ACKs mismatch, and changing the auto-generated ACK is unclear.

title: HTTP Listener flexibility: shared ports/paths, request metadata, binary and custom responses
summary: Each HTTP channel needs its own port, request metadata and headers are hard to reach, multipart and binary support is limited, and custom auth cannot set status codes or bodies.

title: HTTP Sender auth: OAuth 2.0 tokens, preemptive auth, separate proxy credentials
summary: Users hand-roll OAuth token fetching, want preemptive basic auth by default, distinct proxy credentials, NTLM/Kerberos/JWT, and a response status code variable (added in 4.5.2).

title: Email connectors: OAuth for Exchange Online and SMTP reliability
summary: Basic auth to Exchange Online stopped working and OAuth for mail was requested; SMTP intermittently lost mailcap handlers; signatures and dynamic addresses are awkward.

title: JMS connector breakage (ActiveMQ, commons-collections, durable topics)
summary: JMS Sender failed on missing commons-collections 3 in 3.10, the listener stopped working with ActiveMQ in 4.5, and durable topics did not reconnect after broker restarts.

title: SOAP Web Service connectors break on newer Java and leak memory
summary: On Java 17/21 the SAAJ factory is missing and "Get Operations" fails with auth; the sender and listener have memory leaks; javax.jws classes are unavailable for custom services.

title: Database Reader robustness (empty sets, DB reboots, column order, huge schemas)
summary: The reader logs errors on empty result sets, floods NPEs after the database restarts, reordered columns, cached stale URLs, and the table browser stalls on large schemas.

title: Connection pooling for Database Reader/Writer
summary: Database connectors open and close a connection per message, causing millions of connections a day and "too many open files"; users want pooled DB resources with exposed pool settings.
quote: mirth connect creates and drops a new DB connection for every message processed.

title: Connectors hang and cannot be stopped or halted
summary: Database readers, FTP readers and web-service senders stuck on a socket ignore stop and halt, queues back up indefinitely, and only a server restart recovers.

title: Parallel message processing within a single channel
summary: Since 3.x a channel processes one message at a time through filters/transformers; stateless HTTP/query channels and many-connection TCP listeners bottleneck, and users clone channels behind load balancers. Per-connection ordering with concurrent transforms is the ask.
quote: this can severely hamper message throughput

title: Let a transformer set a destination's status (queue, skip, filter, sent)
summary: When a dependency (token, lookup) is unavailable, users want to queue or skip a destination from the transformer instead of forcing a connector error; JavaScript Writers should report a meaningful SENT status.

title: Track message provenance when routing between channels
summary: router.routeMessage does not record the source channel, chained channels lose the full source history, and Channel Writers cannot inject source map values; an OIE fork PR fixed the first.

title: Response processing hooks (postprocessor responses, response processor scripts, multiple responses)
summary: Users want to build the response in the postprocessor or a global response script, filter/transform destination responses, and handle multiple responses from one TCP destination.

title: Duplicate message detection
summary: Users ask how to drop duplicate inbound messages; there is no built-in idempotency check.

title: Control channels from scripts (start/stop/redeploy other channels)
summary: Users want script-level APIs to start channels, restart the service or read server info without calling the REST API.

title: Index and search custom metadata columns quickly (regex, LIKE, IN lists)
summary: Custom metadata searches are slow because columns are unindexed and the query shape defeats indexes; users want optional indexes, regex/LIKE/IN operators, reordering, typed display and export of metadata definitions.

title: Message browser search usability (counts, saved filters, no auto-search, correlated results)
summary: Users want total result counts, saved advanced filters, the option not to search on open, searching by a list of IDs, and seeing source messages alongside errored destinations in one search.

title: Attachment handling gaps (export, regex reattach, reattach in responses, usable tokens)
summary: Attachments cannot be exported from the browser, reinserted with transformations, or attached to responses; expanded attachment tokens are hard to build, and dangling attachments remain when storage is off.

title: Data pruner and archiver improvements
summary: Requests: keep errored messages by default, sub-day retention, block-size limits to avoid OOM, faster archiving of big channels, extensible pruning and reminders when the global pruner is off.

title: Granular per-destination message storage settings
summary: Storage mode applies per channel; users want to store some content types or connectors and not others to save space.

title: Backend database friction (deadlocks, Derby default, partitioning, indexing)
summary: Users hit deadlocks on MySQL/SQL Server, Oracle driver errors, unwanted indexes, huge SQL Server logs and pain leaving Derby; they ask for MySQL partitioning and alternatives such as H2 or CockroachDB.

title: Recover automatically from backend database outages and failovers
summary: Losing the backend DB connection requires a server restart, startup fails instead of retrying, and after an Azure Postgres failover the engine kept connections to the read-only node and hung.

title: Queue visibility and control (per-destination counts, last error, thread assignment)
summary: Users cannot easily see queue depth per destination or why a queued message keeps failing; queues persisted after switching to "never queue", and advanced queue settings are confusing.

title: Reprocessing semantics (detect reprocessed messages, preserve order, avoid double reprocess)
summary: Scripts cannot tell a message is a reprocess, imported messages lose order, and a UI bug reprocessed messages twice.

title: Show last-message time per channel and alert on silent interfaces
summary: Teams monitoring hundreds of channels need last-sent/received timestamps and "no message in N minutes" alerts; today they query per-channel tables, which is slow in production.
quote: We are currently at 228 channels, but this will increase over time.

title: Alerting flexibility (custom variables, message IDs, plugin actions, flood control)
summary: Alerts lack custom template variables and message IDs, cannot be extended with new actions, flood recipients, and sendAlert from some connectors never matched.

title: Statistics are lost or misleading
summary: Upgrading 4.0 to 4.1 wiped statistics, error counts drop when messages are removed, and users want to clear stats except errors.

title: Per-message end-to-end latency metric
summary: Users want received-to-completed milliseconds stored per message and shown on the dashboard so slow messages can be found.

title: Per-channel logs instead of one interleaved server log
summary: With hundreds of channels the dashboard log is flooded; users want logs per channel or tagged with channel, consistent transformer logging, and the ability to restart logging subsystems.

title: Health checks and resource metrics for load balancers and monitoring tools
summary: Users ask for a health URL for AWS ELB/Docker, heap monitoring, SNMP or similar, and easier remote JMX; community built a mobile monitoring app.

title: Server memory leaks and OutOfMemory on large files/queries
summary: Leaks in web-service and SMB connectors and OOMs from large SFTP files, archive queries and pruning non-contiguous IDs.

title: Slow startup, deploy and API calls at scale
summary: High CPU on startup, slow statistics loading and "redeploy all", a channel status API about 20x slower after 4.3, and no way to order startup deployment by tag.

title: Open-source high availability / active-active clustering
summary: Clustering requires the paid Advanced Clustering plugin, which breaks advanced alerting and errors at load; without it two nodes on one DB do not share deployments. Users want active-active, per-channel polling ownership and node visibility.

title: Share global maps across cluster nodes
summary: In a cluster, globalMap values such as a bearer token exist only on the node that set them; users want a replicated map.

title: Deterministic, diff-friendly channel/config exports
summary: Exports reorder sets (library dependencies, enabled channel IDs) and bump revisions on trivial changes, so diffs in source control are noisy; users wrote XSLT normalizers and community patches.
quote: This issue is a real pain for anyone trying to version control their Mirth code.

title: Native Git / source control and CI/CD for channels
summary: Teams want channels in Git with commit comments, push on deploy and CI/CD pipelines; today they rely on community tools (mirthsync, git-ext) or the paid Channel History extension.

title: Promote channels and code templates between environments
summary: Moving channels dev to prod and seeding Docker images with channels is manual; a community "Mirth Migrator" exists, and config map imports should not delete existing keys.

title: Automated and granular backup/restore
summary: Users want scheduled full backups to a directory and selective backup/restore of parts of the config; restore of a backup produced negative revision deltas.

title: Configuration map improvements (groups, DB storage default, variables everywhere)
summary: Users want grouped config keys, database storage by default, $cfg working in every connector field (including timeouts) and structured values.

title: Layered config: local overrides for mirth.properties and vmoptions
summary: Upgrades overwrite mirth.properties and vmoptions, so local edits must be reapplied by hand; users want an override file, standard includes and a startup check for conflicting JVM options.

title: Container/Kubernetes-friendly configuration via environment variables
summary: Users want admin credentials, server and environment names and DB settings from env vars, and smoother Docker upgrades and replicas.

title: Run the Administrator through reverse proxies and load balancers
summary: The JNLP codebase URL is fixed by the server, so launching the Administrator through a reverse proxy or non-root context path fails; POST through a load balancer also broke.

title: Installers that run as a non-privileged user and behave in automation
summary: The Linux service runs as root, Windows installs nag about non-Program Files paths, macOS installers lack notarization, and silent installs hang or fail.

title: Clone/import channels with all their dependencies
summary: Cloned or imported channels lose channel dependencies, code template library links and group membership, and duplicated destinations reuse IDs, so copies silently break.

title: REST API bugs and gaps (JSON vs XML, required params, message search)
summary: JSON responses fail where XML works, Swagger omits required parameters causing NPEs, step sequenceNumber is ignored on POST, and limiting or searching messages via the API is unclear.

title: CLI coverage for code templates and plugins
summary: The CLI only bulk-imported/exported code templates, could not load plugin JARs, and allowed invalid templates in.

title: Ship patched dependencies; scanners flag many high/critical CVEs
summary: Grype, Snyk and Nessus scans of releases report many outdated libraries (jQuery 1.x, commons-text, Xerces). Users ask for timely upgrades; 4.5 was largely a dependency refresh released via test drops.

title: Move off EOL log4j 1.x (Log4Shell scare)
summary: Log4j 1.2.16 (EOL 2015) lingered in the server and closed-source launcher, blocking compliance (UK Cyber Essentials) and GELF shipping; the log4j2 migration left inconsistent logger classes.

title: Publish an SBOM
summary: Users want a CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM per component so they can triage CVEs precisely, citing FDA medical-device SBOM expectations.

title: Patch critical RCE (CVE-2023-43208) for older versions
summary: An unauthenticated remote code execution flaw left users on older versions asking for backported fixes rather than forced upgrades.

title: Stronger password storage and policy, account unlock
summary: User password hashing was weak until 4.4 moved to PBKDF2/Argon2; users still want configurable policy, account unlock and safe special-character handling.

title: Encrypt secrets and sensitive data (channel credentials, config map, attachments, metadata)
summary: Connector passwords export in plain text, the config map is unencrypted, attachments and metadata lacked encryption, and a key encryptor could lose data; users want vault/secret-manager integration.

title: Modern authentication: SSO, MFA, domain accounts, robust LDAP
summary: LDAP login is case-sensitive and buggy, the launcher cannot use domain accounts, and users ask for Duo MFA and SSO.

title: Role-based access control in the free edition
summary: Fine-grained permissions require the paid User Authorization extension; users lost profiles on upgrade and found the RBAC plugin missing in 4.5.

title: Audit and PHI access events
summary: Users want PHI-view events that actually fire, audit entries for message exports, and channel/message IDs in the event log.

title: Lock down exposed web surfaces (Swagger UI, webadmin directories)
summary: Users ask how to disable Swagger UI, restrict webadmin static paths, set CORS headers and fix untrusted certificate findings.

title: Mirth Connect went closed-source/commercial at 4.6
summary: From 4.6 (2025) NextGen stopped publishing releases to GitHub; open-source users stuck on 4.5.2 cannot get upgrade help, and some move to forks such as Open Integration Engine or BridgeLink.
quote: Nextgen will not be releasing anything to github from this point on.

title: Paid-extension licensing is hostile to containers and offline sites
summary: Commercial extensions phone a license server: no offline activation for restricted networks, poor proxy support, licenses consumed by ephemeral containers, and the engine refuses to start without a license.

title: Core capabilities locked behind paid extensions
summary: Channel history/diff, SSL management, clustering, advanced alerting, RBAC and DICOM extras are commercial add-ons, pushing users to community or self-built alternatives.

title: Open-source license compliance gaps (closed jars, wrong license docs)
summary: mirth-crypto.jar shipped without source under MPL-2.0, docs cited the wrong license, and building from source lacked license files present in official builds.

title: Mandatory vendor registration for the first user (4.1)
summary: Version 4.1 forced first-user registration with personal details, which users called invasive for open-source software and awkward under HIPAA minimum-necessary norms.

title: Open-source the Administrator Launcher
summary: The launcher is free but closed, so the community cannot fix its bugs (freezes, outdated log4j, connection sharing) and it has no public release notes; a community replacement (Ballista) appeared.

title: Responsive, community-governed development
summary: Contributors asked for review timelines on PRs and pre-release testing access; hundreds of issues were bulk-closed for inactivity and the Jira import dumped 4,400 issues at once. The OIE fork later took community PRs.

title: Public, accurate documentation
summary: User guides carried "Private and Confidential" footers, wiki links broke, Slack registration was down, old-version docs vanished, client API docs are missing and tooltips misdescribe fields.

title: Generate documentation from channels
summary: Teams want auto-generated docs of filters, transformers and destinations for review, plus a reporting extract of channels/tags and a DB schema viewer.

title: Dark mode for the Administrator
summary: Long-standing request for a dark theme following the OS setting; locked-down organizations cannot rebuild the client to change colors.
quote: not having Dark Mode in the UI is killing me

title: Readable UI on HiDPI screens; configurable font sizes
summary: The Swing client ignores OS scaling, fonts are tiny on 4K displays, Linux needs GDK_SCALE hacks, and 4.5 introduced new DPI scaling bugs.

title: Administrator breaks on macOS/Apple Silicon and newer Java
summary: Monterey and Sonoma crashed or froze the client, Java 17 broke list selection on M1/M2, and users cycled through JVMs with JavaFX to find one that worked.

title: Replace the Java desktop client with a web-based admin UI
summary: The web admin is a thin dashboard; users ask for a fuller browser UI or at least a modern client toolkit, avoiding Java Web Start/launcher dependencies.

title: Administrator Launcher slow/unreliable startup (OCSP storms, offline delays)
summary: The launcher verifies every JAR online with hundreds of threads, triggering firewall SYN-flood alarms and long hangs on servers without internet access.

title: Launcher distrusts properly signed plugins
summary: Extensions signed with CA-issued or private-CA code-signing certificates still trigger untrusted warnings or fail, and accepted certificates are not remembered.

title: Launcher conveniences (JVM args, saved credentials, groups, per-user connections, version info)
summary: Users want per-connection JVM args and logins, folders for many servers, per-user connection files, visible launcher/JVM versions, site icons and a way to silence update prompts.

title: Administrator hangs on network loss and leaks memory when left open
summary: A dropped VPN freezes the client so it cannot even close, idle sessions time out on first requests, and long-open clients leak heap.

title: Edits lost or overwritten (code templates, transformer steps, concurrent users)
summary: Code templates lost code after sorting, moving transformer steps overwrote other steps in 4.5, saving one destination rewrote others, and simultaneous editors silently clobber each other; users want edit locks.

title: Validate channel configuration before save
summary: The editor lets users save undeployable filter logic and duplicate template functions, and does not show which fields take a map key versus a value.

title: Multiple windows and cross-channel navigation in the Administrator
summary: Comparing two channels or reading code while browsing messages requires logging in twice; users also want to follow channel-writer links between channels from the dashboard.

title: Show listening ports and port usage in channel lists
summary: Finding a free port takes many clicks; users want a ports column and a reliable in-use list (which broke when a port was a variable).

title: Channel grouping and organization
summary: Groups arrived in 3.x but users want nesting, collapse-all, revision roll-ups, destination-level filtering; channels have disappeared from or duplicated in groups.

title: Smoother edit-deploy workflow
summary: Deploy jumps to the dashboard, cannot be done from the editor or per connector, and non-default scripts are not flagged.

title: Transformer step editing ergonomics
summary: Moving steps one position at a time is slow; users want move to top/bottom, insert-below, step import/export and sortable mappings.

title: Keyboard shortcuts and copy/paste throughout the UI
summary: Copying variables, IDs and search text needs right-click options or is impossible; expand/collapse lacks shortcuts.

title: Localization and international formats (Chinese UI, 24-hour time)
summary: Users request a Chinese UI and fonts, and complain that logs show 12-hour timestamps.

title: Configurable defaults for new channels
summary: Users want default data types and channel settings applied to every new channel.

title: Java version upgrades break the engine (Java 9+ module access, 16/17/21)
summary: Each new Java release broke internals (CachedRowSet, Rhino MemberBox, JDBC), requiring --add-opens incantations, while Java 8 support lingered; users want clean support for current LTS JDKs.

title: Version upgrades break channels, plugins and settings
summary: Upgrades have failed to start, refused old channel exports, caused classloading conflicts, lost statistics and user profiles, broke PDF writers and Web Start access.

title: Make plugin development easier and stable
summary: Plugin APIs break without notice, views such as the message table are not pluggable, column plugins threw NPEs, and plugins cannot declare compatible server versions.

title: AI assistance inside the engine
summary: Users float AI plugins and agent-style behavior; community members build modern HL7/FHIR editors for debugging.
